Q3587182.label: 1976 Jamaican general election
Q3587182.summary: General elections were held in Jamaica on 15 December 1976. The result was a victory for the People's National Party, which won 47 of the 60 seats. Voter turnout was 85%.

Q840814.label: Les Engagés
Q840814.summary: Les Engagés is a centrist French-speaking political party in Belgium. The party originated in the split in 1972 of the unitary Christian Social Party (PSC-CVP), which had been the country's governing party for much of the post-war period. It continued to be called the Christian Social Party until 2002 when it was renamed the Humanist Democratic Centre. It took its current name on 17 March 2022, and currently is a member of the governing national coalition in Belgium, along with the Walloon and French Community coalition governments.

Q316526.label: Vladimír Mečiar
Q316526.summary: Vladimír Mečiar is a Slovak former politician who served as the prime minister of Slovakia from June 1990 to May 1991, June 1992 to March 1994, and again from December 1994 to October 1998. He was the leader of the Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), a populist party in Slovakia.

Q2069102.label: 1998 Maltese general election
Q2069102.summary: General elections were held in Malta on 5 September 1998. The result was a victory for the Nationalist Party, which won 35 of the 65 seats.

Q2665070.label: Jozo Križanović
Q2665070.summary: Jozo Križanović was a Bosnian politician who served as the Croat member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 2001 to 2002. A member of the Social Democratic Party, he later served in the national House of Representatives from 2002 to 2009.

Q7541870.label: Slovenian privatisation referendum, 2003
Q7541870.summary: A referendum on privatisation was held in Slovenia on 19 January 2003. Voters were asked whether Slovenian Railways should be kept as a single company during the privatisation process and whether subscribers to Telekom Slovenije should receive a rebate for the above market price fees paid for cable TV prior to privatisation.

Q5450862.label: 1962 Finnish presidential election
Q5450862.summary: Two-stage presidential elections were held in Finland in 1962. On 15 and 16 January the public elected presidential electors to an electoral college. They in turn elected the President. The result was a victory for Urho Kekkonen, who won on the first ballot. The turnout for the popular vote was 81.5%.

Q123139694.label: killing of Ahmed Yassin
Q123139694.summary: On 22 March 2004, the Palestinian leader and one of the founders of Hamas, Ahmed Yassin, aged 67, was assassinated in Gaza City. Sheikh Ahmed Yassin – who used a wheelchair due to being quadriplegic since his adolescence – was returning from performing the Fajr prayer, and his companions were also killed immediately.

Q29001838.label: 2017 Westminster attack
Q29001838.desc: terror attack which occurred on 22 March 2017 in Westminster, Greater London, England, UK
Q29001838.summary: On 22 March 2017, a terrorist attack took place outside the Palace of Westminster in London, seat of the British Parliament. Khalid Masood, a 52-year-old Briton, drove a car into pedestrians on the pavement along the south side of Westminster Bridge and Bridge Street, injuring more than 50 people, four of them fatally.

Q279662.label: Cristero War
Q279662.desc: widespread struggle in many central-western Mexican states from 1926 to 1929
Q279662.summary: The Cristero War, also known as the Cristero Rebellion or La Cristiada, was a widespread struggle in central and western Mexico from 3 August 1926 to 21 June 1929 in response to the implementation of secularist and anticlerical articles of the 1917 Constitution. The rebellion was instigated as a response to an executive decree by Mexican President Plutarco Elías Calles to strictly enforce Article 130 of the Constitution, an implementing act known as the Calles Law.

Q446574.label: Anna Schwartz
Q446574.summary: Anna Jacobson Schwartz was an American economist and monetary historian who worked at the National Bureau of Economic Research for more than seven decades. Paul Krugman has said that Schwartz is "one of the world's greatest monetary scholars."
